audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text attributes Mega Gnar's stun to Boulder Toss: "GNAR! (R) wall-slam plus Boulder Toss stun". Boulder Toss is Mega Gnar's Q and it slows. The Mega stun is Wallop, his W.
audit.why: Riot's Q text says the boulder damages and slows everything nearby; the stun lives on W — "Mega Gnar ... can rear up on his hind legs and smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies in an area". A Zac player told the stun comes off the thrown boulder will misread which cast to dodge, and Wallop is the one that actually locks him for the follow-up.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (Q Boulder Toss: slow; W Wallop: hardCC)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] listed "A sidewall to slam him into after your engage" as something Zac wants. Zac has no wall interaction anywhere in his kit.
audit.why: The wall-slam in this matchup belongs to Gnar, not Zac: GNAR! stuns and deals bonus damage to enemies thrown into terrain. None of Zac's abilities carry a terrain flag — Q throws two enemies together, E and R knock up, and none of them gain anything from a wall. The entry gave the player a capability they do not have, and worse, it points them toward exactly the terrain that makes Gnar's ultimate stronger against them.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real positioning rule — fight in open ground so his R cannot wall-stun you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged no cooldown-sequencing advice, and the full layer compounds it by naming GNAR! as the cooldown to track in six places — breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[5].why and dosFull[0].
audit.why: GNAR! is not gated by its cooldown in practice; it is gated by the Rage bar and by being in Mega form at all. Telling a player to engage "once GNAR! is down" describes the wrong clock entirely — Gnar can be harmless in mini form with the ultimate technically available, or lethal the moment his bar fills. The content layer already gets this right in wants.you[0] ("Gnar's Rage bar empty (mini form) before you E in"), so the two layers were teaching different things.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed the full layer at the Rage bar and added the two real cooldowns: Wallop at 7s and Hop at 22s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hop was never mentioned as a punish window.
audit.why: Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s and is mini-Gnar's only escape. At rank 1 that is a 22-second window in which a Zac who forces him to burn it can walk him down — longer than Zac's own Elastic Slingshot at 21s. This is the single most concrete wait-for-X-before-Y line available in the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Added Hop 22s as the engage trigger.

audit.whatIsWrong: The layers disagree on three stages: content reads Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Zac/Gnar/Skill/Zac, full reads Gnar/Skill/Zac/Zac/Gnar/Zac/Zac.
audit.why: The content chart is the accurate one. Mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw is 1100 range against Zac's 800-range Q, so he genuinely owns levels 1-3, and the content layer's own spikes[0] says "your first real window is level 4". The full layer handed Zac levels 2 and 3 in the exact phase where he is out-ranged by 300 units.
audit.corrected: Aligned the full layer to the content chart.

notes: The content layer for this matchup is genuinely good — it tracks the Rage bar, mini versus Mega, and the wall stun. The full layer is the problem: it names GNAR! as the cooldown to track in six separate strings, which is the wrong clock. Gnar's threat is gated by Rage and by which form he is in, not by his ultimate's cooldown, so "engage once GNAR! is down" is unactionable in the same way the Gangplank entry's "engage when Powder Keg is down" was. Two content errors worth flagging beyond the edits: the Mega stun was credited to Boulder Toss when it belongs to Wallop, and wants.you[1] told the player to look for "a sidewall to slam him into" — Zac has no terrain interaction at all, and the wall in this matchup is Gnar's win condition, not Zac's. That one actively steers a player toward the terrain that makes GNAR! stun them. NOT VERIFIED, left untouched: full.tldr says "His %HP hurts" and dontsFull[2] says "Stack pure HP vs %damage". Gnar's kit carries no percentHealth flag anywhere in champ-data/_kits/gnar.json, so I could not confirm those claims from the data on disk. I did not edit them either way — Hyper may well deal max-health damage and I would rather leave a possibly-correct line alone than assert its removal. Worth a targeted check.
